headline: LLM agents generate and code-verify biological analysis methods and discoveries
label: Verified Llm Research Agents
summary: Recent preprints and two published papers report LLM agent systems that automate bioinformatics, sequencing, and spatial omics analysis with verification.
synthesis: The dominant thread is LLM-driven agents that translate biological questions into executable analysis workflows, with verification built into the process. PRAXIS distills cases, rules and skills into memory to guide method selection and code-verified validation. BioGAIP and NanoCortex package multi-agent LLM systems for bioinformatics pipelines and nanopore sequencing, from basecalling through biological interpretation. SpatialClaw pairs 30 spatial omics skills with graph-based persistent memory, benchmarked on 10 skills. Robin automates hypothesis generation and data analysis, reporting ripasudil as an in vitro candidate for dry AMD, while ERA pairs an LLM with tree search to generate scientific software, reporting 40 new single-cell analysis methods outperforming human ones. What is new is the shift from agents as assistants to agents as producers of verified methods and discoveries. Evidence here is largely system descriptions and does not yet establish comparative generalization across tasks.
